name: Bamako
subtitle: Bamako, capital of Mali: its numbers, a short history and places to see beyond the World Heritage list.

keyPoints.text: About 4,227,569 people live in the District of Bamako (preliminary 2022 census) (counted 2022).
Bamako comes from the Bambara for 'marigot du crocodile' (crocodile backwater), and was founded at the end of the 16th century by the Niaré, formerly called Niakaté, originally Sarakolé.
The three crocodiles that symbolise Bamako come from the three backwaters (Lido, Diafarana and Bèlèsôkô) that once crossed the city and flowed into the Niger.

parts.text: Bamako comes from the Bambara for 'marigot du crocodile' (crocodile backwater), and was founded at the end of the 16th century by the Niaré, formerly called Niakaté, originally Sarakolé.
The three crocodiles that symbolise Bamako come from the three backwaters (Lido, Diafarana and Bèlèsôkô) that once crossed the city and flowed into the Niger.
Niaréla, the Niaré quarter, is one of the oldest districts of Bamako.
The district of Bamako holds 18.9 percent of Mali's population and is the most populous region.
The district of Bamako has an urbanisation rate of 99.7 percent, the highest in Mali.
More than half of Mali's urban population lives in the district of Bamako (62 percent).
The Koulouba palace, built between 1903 and 1907 as the governor's palace, became the seat of the presidency of the Republic at independence in 1960.
The Point G hospital began to be built in 1905.

parts.text: 4,227,569 in 2022, according to the figures compiled from the national statistics office. Which area is counted matters: District of Bamako, resident population at the fifth general census (RGPH5, 2022), preliminary results report published November 2023.

items.text: Bamako was founded by the Niaré (Niakaté), who were originally Sarakolé.
On 1 February French forces led by Borgnis-Desbordes entered Bamako, then a fortified village of 600 inhabitants.
Bamako became the administrative seat (chef-lieu) of a cercle.
Bamako became capital of Haut Sénégal-Niger on 17 October, and of French Sudan in 1920.
The Dakar-Niger railway line was inaugurated.
Koulouba palace became the seat of the presidency of the Republic at independence.
The Grande Mosquée, rebuilt from 1966 with Saudi support, was inaugurated on 30 July by President Moussa Traoré.
The fifth general census (RGPH5) found 4,227,569 residents in the district of Bamako.

blocks.q: Myth or fact: Bamako was already a large city when the French arrived.
blocks.explain: At the end of the 19th century Bamako was a large fortified village of 600 inhabitants when the French entered it on 1 February 1883; the district now has 4,227,569 residents (2022).
